rows.name: @humblelifeskills
rows.evidence: Gave concrete fixes (viewport culling with chunked rendering, macOS App Nap OBS command, Glacier/NAS storage, dedicated encoder hardware) and built a virtual house for the streamer while welcoming and moderating chat, though much output is hype spam and repeated Discord-stat/CNVS plugs.

rows.name: @BrandynMakes
rows.evidence: Gave concrete build advice (explained LOD rendering, server replay recording synced to bug reports, sending distant players fewer updates, Tauri/Electron wrapping, Tailscale/private-network checks, MediaMTX recording) while welcoming newcomers and steering people to the Discord; some messages are banter and command plugs.

rows.name: @slop_enjoyerr
rows.evidence: Real tips (prompt-injection risk in the chat-reading agent, an on-screen chat scroll bug, draw-distance and debug-harness ideas, explaining compaction, the /model command, Opus orchestrating Sonnet) and live release updates, buried under heavy roast banter, repeated 'sell' spam and jabs at another viewer.

rows.name: @oscargalvez7
rows.evidence: Gave actionable suggestions (preventDefault on Tab, a username filter for stream, parachute loot drops, a Three.js performance question, Sonnet subagents in Claude Code) and was consistently welcoming to the streamer and other chatters.

rows.name: @therealkosmicnomad
rows.evidence: Consistently encouraging and constructive: proposed an in-game bug-report bot, solo AI race mode, jetpacks/gliders, reported missing colliders and an AMD loading hang at 64%, and suggested Opus-vs-Sol comparisons.

rows.name: @two6hundo
rows.evidence: Steady stream of constructive ideas: AI triage of bug reports, distance-based rendering optimization, debug/non-scored mode, version number in the menu, ghost runs, play-space instances, and a map-boundary bug report, all delivered with consistent encouragement.

rows.name: @TheZarion007
rows.evidence: Enthusiastic hype man who greets and cheers others and asks casual model questions, but offers almost no technical input and most messages are exclamations.

rows.name: @lepahc
rows.evidence: Offered actionable ideas (memory layer separating user instructions from agent-derived info, DayZ-style item scattering rules, hooking jev up to triage chat ideas, Electron over Tauri) and answered other viewers' questions about agent usage and quotas.

rows.name: @man74s
rows.evidence: Gave concrete workflow advice (run Opus 5.5 as orchestrator and have Claude Code spin off Sonnet 5.5 worker agents, a model-tier breakdown) and flagged audio balance problems to the streamer, amid a lot of OpenAI ribbing.

rows.name: @Superdoopercooper
rows.evidence: Some useful ideas (narrating playtest bugs to a listening CNVS agent, manual prompting over looping) but also a wrong LOD definition, with helpfulness mostly cheering and defending the stream amid many 'lets go' messages.

rows.name: @davidkang5708
rows.evidence: Offered sensible model opinions (Sol as a non-creative backend workhorse, chef/sous-chef agent hierarchy, Opus-vs-Sonnet subagent question, looping suggestions), but helpfulness is dragged down by repeated IQ insults aimed at other viewers.

rows.name: @shonifari
rows.evidence: Flagged that the video audio drowned out the streamer's voice, shared discord commands, pushed back on a patronising chatter, and gave reasonable takes on effort levels, token use and price anchoring, alongside many 'W'/'LFG' messages.

rows.name: @coderanger75
rows.evidence: Gave practical suggestions (lower mic input sensitivity, double-tap mic for dictation, use Sonnet 5.5 on low/med for small bugs, breakdown of new plan usage tiers) mixed with a lot of cynical DevDay commentary.

rows.name: @adrianpadurariu
rows.evidence: Gave actionable debugging tips (check for headless browsers, point to session id, npm run dev, cache warnings) and flagged a possible public IP leak twice, but also sent a burst of fragmented 'dot com' spam and lots of mocking event commentary.

rows.name: @Gnokain
rows.evidence: Gave concrete game/UX feedback (fix missing colliders, put Resume as the top button, fixed loot spawns for competitive play, nerf sniper, a viewer-room idea for streamers) along with lots of questions and short reactions.

rows.name: @GarlicCruton
rows.evidence: Mostly greetings and hype with model name-drops; a few ideas (vendor-neutral optimized harness for CNVS, Jev reviewing transcripts to feed agents) and friendly replies to others.

rows.name: @creepybeat
rows.evidence: Repeatedly reported a concrete inventory ammo-count bug and suggested motion-blur toggle, FPS counter, storm-damage nerf and a storm-cloud gradient, mixed with playful banter.

rows.name: @foschleo
rows.evidence: Gave genuinely useful game-dev advice (radius-based LOD hierarchy to prevent pop-in, a building-planner system, grid-based map generation with per-POI agents), but repeated it many times in all caps alongside SELL spam.

rows.name: @iamdonh
rows.evidence: Offered sensible ideas (stats on model-release posts as a CNVS sales funnel, letting the community run subagents on the VPS) and practical help like a mic-level tip, the DevDay link and noting new plans were live, though many messages are !discord commands and emotes.

rows.name: @of9490
rows.evidence: Gave concrete model-usage comparisons (Opus 5.5 High vs xHigh cost/benefit, Sonnet vs Opus at matched performance, Haiku as a test model) and asked useful engine and isolation questions, though repeated the cynical 'Dots is free for training data' point several times.

rows.name: @yesindeed900
rows.evidence: Cited Artificial Analysis benchmarks on Sonnet cost/intelligence and WebGPU performance issues and posted a screenshot to Discord, but much of the chat is crude hype or dev-day mockery.

rows.name: @Shhhmooke
rows.evidence: Friendly regular with banter and a couple of practical notes (add cash credits and have the agent write a handoff, asks about effort level and three.js), but low technical depth.

rows.name: @HeatStoker69
rows.evidence: Technical input includes storing as JSON before updates, inverted normals as a debugging idea, render-resolution/post-processing notes and effort-level observations; helpfulness is modest feature ideas and questions offset by a long run of cynical event commentary in Stream D.

rows.name: @smellyydeli
rows.evidence: Relayed useful news (Sonnet 5.5 found in the Claude Code binary with version and pricing, the 6.1 delay) and suggested higher effort settings, mixed with hype spam and light trolling.

rows.name: @techtejash6622
rows.evidence: Mostly hype and self-referential questions about pricing their own editor, with heavy spam (14x 'ONE MORE THING' and repeated VOLUME demands) that outweighed the occasional relevant question.

rows.name: @byanuragbaral
rows.evidence: Technical input is limited to a UI overlay suggestion and a token-cost comparison among many spec/ASI questions; helpfulness comes from answering a lag question and friendly engagement, offset by repeated unanswered spec questions.

rows.name: @fooledbyprimes

rows.name: @simonbourdon1018
rows.evidence: Technical input is a repeated 'texture streaming' suggestion and a model-creativity opinion; helpfulness from pointing chat to pricing details in Discord, diluted by many duplicated messages.

rows.name: @RedMir564
rows.evidence: Technical input is limited to light remarks (Steam disclosure, add a save feature to Only Up), while helpfulness comes from warm community support, greeting others and cheering the vibe-coding community.

rows.name: @sumwhat1275
rows.evidence: Technical input is light (route bug reports to Opus, use NVIDIA built-in, model-merging observation); helpfulness is friendly game feedback and greetings rather than active support.

rows.name: @SebBalls-1
rows.evidence: Sharp technical takes (quantization jab, cheaper/faster/better trade-off, Codex CLI fallback, prompting advice) and a warning about env leaks on stream, though largely cynical commentary on the event.

rows.name: @Quigago

rows.name: @CJs-e2c
rows.evidence: Asked reasonable questions (Marshall vs Chase agent roles, video file size and lower resolution, model naming) and ran a poll, but offered little concrete technical input.

rows.name: @apocalipto3343

rows.name: @andreaskrbyravn855

rows.name: @JohnTheDragon
rows.evidence: Near-zero technical input (one 'have claude update itself' quip); helpfulness from audio-level feedback and pointing the streamer to Discord, with most messages being affectionate roasting and running jokes.

rows.name: @why.kabira

rows.name: @DanielsApps2

rows.name: @brunoczr

rows.name: @wsmawm

rows.name: @saurabh.n.sawant

rows.name: @roland7358

rows.name: @luckey_faraday

rows.name: @chaddonnerschwanz7504

rows.name: @Mousebear3

rows.name: @rawgoldranks

rows.name: @brett7277

rows.name: @yokatamin
